title: Care Tips for Refurbished Histology Equipment to Extend Efficiency
description: As laboratories and medical facilities strive to manage their budgets, investing in refurbished histology equipment can be a wise cost-saving choice. These machines, when properly maintained and cared…
content:
Care Tips for Refurbished Histology Equipment to Extend Efficiency
As laboratories and medical facilities strive to manage their budgets, investing in refurbished histology equipment can be a wise cost-saving choice. These machines, when properly maintained and cared for, offer not just efficiency but also excellent value for money. Your role in ensuring the optimal function and extended lifespan of these instruments is crucial. This post will delve into essential tips that empower you to maintain and care for your refurbished histology equipment. I. Regular Cleaning Procedures:
Maintaining cleanliness is paramount when it comes to the operation of any refurbished histology instrument . Here are some simple yet vital cleaning steps that should be performed regularly: Dusting: Use a soft cloth or a fine-bristle brush to gently remove dust from the equipment's surface. This helps prevent dust particles from infiltrating internal components, potentially causing damage. Routine Disinfection: Proper disinfection maintains cleanliness and prevents the transmission of harmful pathogens . Follow manufacturer guidelines to use appropriate cleaning agents targeting bacteria and viruses while protecting the equipment's surface. Filter Replacement: Some histology machines have filters that help maintain air quality within the instrument for optimal performance. These filters accumulate dust and debris over time, so they must be replaced according to the manufacturer's instructions or when they appear excessively clogged. II. Regular Calibration:
Calibration is not just a task, it's a necessity for achieving accurate results from your refurbished histology equipment . Over time, wear and tear or environmental factors might affect instrument calibration, leading to inaccurate measurements or outputs. Regular calibration checks, as per manufacturer recommendations, are the key to maintaining the efficiency of your machine: Scheduled Calibration Checks: It's crucial to adhere strictly to recommended schedules provided by manufacturers for calibration checks—these may vary depending on the specific type of equipment being used. Professional Assistance: Seeking assistance from experts ensures proper calibration. Consider partnering with an authorized service provider specializing in maintaining and repairing histology equipment. Records of Calibration: Keep accurate records of the dates and results of your calibration checks. This will help you identify significant deviations from expected performance, allowing timely intervention and ensuring uninterrupted workflow. III. Proper Service and Maintenance: Regular Inspections: Conduct periodic inspections of the various components of the equipment to identify signs of damage or deterioration. Look out for loose connections, worn-out belts, or cracked tubes needing immediate attention. Lubrication: Many histology instruments have moving parts that require lubrication to ensure smooth operation. Refer to manufacturer guidelines to determine the frequency and type of lubricant suitable for your instrument model. Preventive Service Contracts: Consider obtaining a preventive service contract with an authorized service provider familiar with refurbished histology equipment. These contracts often provide regular scheduled maintenance visits, reducing downtime and prolonging the machine's lifespan. IV. Storage Considerations:
Proper storage is not just a suggestion, it's a significant factor in maintaining your refurbished histology equipment's overall condition and longevity. The right storage conditions, including cleanliness, dryness, and freedom from excessive heat or humidity, can prevent damage to sensitive electronic components and extend the lifespan of your instrument: Environmental Conditions: Ensure the storage area is clean, dry, and free from excessive heat or humidity. Extreme environmental conditions can damage sensitive electronic components and shorten the lifespan of your instrument. Covering Equipment: When not in use, it's advisable to cover your machines appropriately. Dust covers protect against dust buildup, while moisture-resistant covers safeguard against unexpected spills or leaks. V. Trained Staff Education:
In addition to undergoing regular maintenance checks performed by professionals, empowering your staff members with basic knowledge regarding upkeep practices can be beneficial in creating a culture that promotes long-term reliability. Training staff members on proper usage and handling procedures can undoubtedly contribute towards achieving optimal efficiency and an increased operational life span for your refurbished histology equipment. Conclusion:
Looking after your refurbished histology equipment need not be a daunting task; it simply requires discipline and regular maintenance practices. By diligently following the tips outlined in this post, you can significantly extend the lifespan of your machines, ensuring optimal performance for a longer period. A well-maintained instrument translates to precise results, increased efficiency, and reduced operating costs for your laboratory or medical facility. Your commitment to proper care today will yield substantial benefits tomorrow.

title: 10 Signs You Are Struggling with Cocaine Addiction and How to Seek Help
description: Cocaine addiction is a serious issue that affects people from all walks of life. Unfortunately, recognizing the signs of addiction in yourself or a loved one can be challenging. In this featured post,…
content:
Photo by MART PRODUCTION from Pexels.com
Cocaine addiction is a serious issue that affects people from all walks of life. Unfortunately, recognizing the signs of addiction in yourself or a loved one can be challenging. In this featured post, we will explore ten common indicators of cocaine addiction and provide guidance on how to seek help. 1. Neglected Responsibilities
One telltale sign of struggling with cocaine addiction is neglecting essential responsibilities in various areas of life, such as work, relationships, or personal health. Those struggling with addiction may find themselves constantly preoccupied with obtaining and using cocaine, leading to decreased productivity and deteriorating relationships. 2. Physical Symptoms
The physical symptoms associated with cocaine abuse can range from mild to severe. These may include an extreme boost in energy followed by intense crashes, dilated pupils, weight loss due to reduced appetite, significant night sweats impacting sleep quality, increased heart rate and blood pressure levels, and frequent nosebleeds if the drug is snorted regularly. 3. Financial Difficulties
Cocaine addiction is both psychologically and financially draining. Individuals spending excessive amounts on maintaining their habits often face considerable financial difficulties. They may struggle to pay bills on time, experience mounting debt, or even resort to theft or other unethical activities as the desperation grows. 4. Relationship Strain
Substance abuse can put a strain on even the strongest bonds between individuals. Those addicted to cocaine often have challenges maintaining healthy relationships because their focus becomes centered on acquiring their next dose rather than nurturing connections with loved ones. Tension grows as trust starts diminishing due to broken promises or deceptive behavior relating to drug use. 5. Behavioral Changes
Cocaine addiction often leads to behavioral alterations that are easily observed by close contacts. Individuals might exhibit increased irritability and restlessness, particularly when not using the drug. There's often a stark decline in how they manage their personal hygiene and overall appearance. Furthermore, their demeanor may shift towards displaying overly confident behaviors, which can sometimes cross into aggression or result in unpredictable mood swings. These signs highlight the profound impact cocaine has on a person's behavior and emotional regulation. 6. Social Withdrawal
Addiction, particularly to substances like cocaine, fundamentally alters the social behaviors and interpersonal relationships of individuals. As the compelling need to consume the drug intensifies, efforts to conceal its detrimental effects become futile, leading to increased isolation. The stigma and shame associated with addiction, coupled with the physical and psychological grip of the substance, encourage those affected to retreat from social engagement.
They might decline invitations, miss significant milestones, or choose to be alone, prioritizing substance use over connecting with others. This pattern of social withdrawal not only exacerbates the isolation but also impedes recovery efforts, creating a vicious cycle of loneliness and dependency. 7. Health Deterioration
Prolonged cocaine abuse can lead to severe health issues. Some prevalent health problems associated with addiction include cardiovascular complications, liver and kidney damage, respiratory issues such as chronic cough or wheezing occasionally accompanied by chest pains, and increased vulnerability to infections. In such situations, treating the physical illness becomes as important as identifying and treating the addiction issue. 8. Failed Attempts at Quitting
Many individuals struggling with cocaine addiction realize its harmful impact on their lives and make attempts to quit. However, the grip of addiction is strong, making sustainable recovery challenging without professional assistance. If you or a loved one have made multiple unsuccessful efforts at quitting cocaine use independently, it's essential to seek help for more effective treatment options tailored to individual needs. 9. Emotional Instability
Cocaine abuse directly affects brain chemistry and can disrupt emotion regulation systems over time. Mood swings become more frequent; feelings of euphoria give way to deep depression during withdrawal phases. Individuals suffering from cocaine addiction experience emotional instability that hinders their ability to lead a fulfilling life and foster healthy relationships. 10. Increased Tolerance
As dependency develops, individuals often need larger doses of cocaine to achieve the desired effects due to acquired tolerance. If you find yourself continually increasing your dosage or needing more frequent access to sustain similar effects as before – this may be indicative of an escalating problem requiring intervention. Conclusion
Recognizing the signs of cocaine addiction is the first step toward seeking proper assistance. If you or someone you know resonates with any of those ten indicators discussed, do not hesitate to reach out to professionals experienced in helping individuals recover from addiction. There are rehabilitation centers offering a variety of treatment options for patients. By seeking timely support, one can begin their journey towards lasting recovery and living a healthier, happier life free from substance abuse.

title: A Guide to Composting
description: By Laurel Aiello | Fort Collins Nursery DIY composting turns organic waste into nutrients for your garden while reducing your carbon footprint. It also saves you money on store-bought garden…
content:
Compost (Photo from Pixabay.com)
By Laurel Aiello | Fort Collins Nursery
DIY composting turns organic waste into nutrients for your garden while reducing your carbon footprint. It also saves you money on store-bought garden amendments, which add up quickly if you have a lot of beds to fill or land to till. However, there's more to composting than tossing yard waste and food scraps into a tub in the backyard. Here are some basics to get you started.
Compost (Photo from Pixabay.com)
What to Compost
Compost bins are especially appealing in the summer when there are lots of fresh food scraps, weeds, and tree and shrub trimmings to dispose of. In a home composter, only kitchen scraps without meat, dairy, fat, and oil should be composted to avoid introducing bacteria to your garden (though some local composting services do accept these items).
Fruit and vegetable scraps, crushed egg shells, used tea bags, and coffee grounds add moisture and nitrogen—a critical nutrient for leafy plant growth—to your compost pile, as does green lawn waste. Mix in fresh grass clippings, live twigs and branches, weeds without seeds, wilted cut flowers, and other plant material that is quick to decompose. You can think of these as 'green' compost ingredients.
'Brown' materials are also critical as they provide carbon to feed the microorganisms decomposing your organic waste. Examples are brown paper bags, wax-free cardboard, straw, wood chips, pine needles, dry leaves, mulch, and sawdust from untreated wood. These ingredients also bulk up your compost pile, creating airflow to help the food scraps and fresh yard waste break down.
The right balance of green and brown materials ensures that your compost pile will properly heat up and decompose without rotting or smelling foul. A ratio of approximately four brown ingredients to one green ingredient is typically recommended, though it doesn't have to be exact. Compost Bin (Photo from Pixabay.com)
Composter Types
There are lots of different types of home composters, including countertop compost bins, backyard composters and vermicomposters that use earthworms for decomposition. Though these containers all produce compost, there are some things to consider before you invest in one.
Outdoor compost bins are either active or passive. Active composters require manual turning with a pitchfork about every four days—though there are compost tumblers with hand cranks that make it easier—and the compost can be gathered directly inside the bin. Passive compost bins with proper ventilation allow you to add ingredients to the top without turning the pile, producing aged compost at the bottom. Though passive systems offer a hands-off approach, they are slower to produce than active systems, and collecting the finished product can be more difficult.
Indoor compost bins make it easy to collect food scraps throughout the week so you don't have to run every banana peel and carrot top to your outdoor composter. These are handy if you live in an apartment or townhome and want to compost on a small scale, and they seal shut to trap odors. Worm bins are also available at your local garden center or can be a fun DIY project—just do your research to avoid bringing unwanted pests into your home. Compost Bin (Photo from Pixabay.com)

title: How to Prove Medical Negligence and File a Medical Malpractice Claim
description: Medical malpractice occurs when a patient is harmed by a medical professional who fails to perform their duties competently. This can include a doctor failing to diagnose what is wrong, administering…
content:
Medical malpractice occurs when a patient is harmed by a medical professional who fails to perform their duties competently. This can include a doctor failing to diagnose what is wrong, administering improper treatment, or not warning the patient of a treatment's known risks. According to the state's rules, the patient should file a claim against the medical professional for such malpractice.
Each state has its own rules about medical malpractice, including whether you need to notify the physician first and when to bring the lawsuit. However, there are general and broad categories of rules that most medical malpractice cases follow. This is why consulting an experienced and reputed lawyer like attorney Russell Berkowitz of Berkowitz Hanna Malpractice & Injury Lawyers is always a good idea .
This article will consider some basic requirements for filing a medical malpractice claim. There Must Have Been a Doctor-Patient Relationship
To initiate a medical malpractice claim, the patient needs to establish a physician-patient relationship with the doctor being sued. This typically involves an explicit agreement between the two parties, such as a discussion between the patient and the doctor regarding the latter's services.
It is easier to prove the existence of a doctor-patient relationship if the doctor has begun seeing and treating you. However, if the consulting medical professional did not treat you directly, there may be questions about whether or not a relationship exists. Medical Negligence Must Be Proven Beyond a Doubt
It is not enough to be unhappy with your doctor's treatment methods or the treatment results. Proving that the doctor was negligent in their diagnosis and treatment is key for a medical malpractice claim. Proving medical negligence means you show that the doctor harmed you in a way that a 'reasonable doctor' would not have in the same situation.
The doctor does not have to be the best possible, but they must be 'reasonably skillful and careful.' A doctor's reasonable skillfulness and carefulness are often the major topics of discussion in a medical malpractice claim. The patient is typically required to present a medical expert to discuss the right medical standard of care. Then, they will show how the defendant's physician deviated from this standard. The Injury Must Have Directly Resulted from the Physician's Negligence
The possibility of a doctor's negligence resulting in the injury is always considered in these cases. For instance, if a patient died after being treated for lung cancer , and the doctor was negligent, it can be hard to prove that the patient's death was due to the doctor's negligence rather than cancer. Therefore, the patient must show that the doctor's incompetence 'more likely than not' directly caused the injury. Almost all states will require that the patient have a medical expert testify against the doctor. These experts have the professional acumen and reputation necessary to offer credible opinions by evaluating all the factors. The Injury Must Have Resulted in Certain Damages
A medical malpractice claim is invalid if the patient did not suffer any harm or injury, even if the doctor was found to have been negligent. That is, even if it is evident that the doctor performed below their field's expected standard, the patient could not sue for malpractice unless the doctor actually caused them harm.
In case the damages are proven, the patient can seek compensation for various types of harm in a medical malpractice lawsuit. This includes lost wages, reduced earning potential, mental distress, physical pain, and any additional medical expenses incurred. Conclusion
A complex body of rules governs and regulates medical malpractice law, and this varies from one state to another. There are also various factors involved in satisfactorily proving medical negligence beyond a doubt. Hence, if you are filing a medical malpractice claim, consider hiring a seasoned medical malpractice attorney for trusted legal advice and representation. They will handle the legal complexities on your behalf and provide invaluable advice and guidance every step of the way while fighting to uphold justice.

title: 5 Cases of Bird Flu Reported in Colorado Poultry Workers, Doubling This Year's US Tally
author: Amy Maxmen
description: Amy Maxmen | KFF Health News July 15, 2024 Five people who work at a poultry farm in northeastern Colorado have tested positive for the bird flu, the Colorado public health department reported July…
content:
(Photo by Blaine Howerton) Amy Maxmen | KFF Health News
July 15, 2024
Five people who work at a poultry farm in northeastern Colorado have tested positive for the bird flu, the Colorado public health department reported July 14. This brings the known number of U.S. cases to nine.
The five people were likely infected by chickens, which they had been tasked with killing in response to a bird flu outbreak at the farm.
More than 99 million chickens and turkeys have been infected with a highly pathogenic strain of the bird flu that emerged at U.S. poultry farms in early 2022. Since then, the federal government has compensated poultry farmers more than $1 billion for destroying infected flocks and eggs to keep outbreaks from spreading.
The H5N1 bird flu virus has spread among poultry farms around the world for nearly 30 years. An estimated 900 people have been infected by birds, and roughly half have died from the disease.
The virus made an unprecedented shift this year to dairy cattle in the U.S. This poses a higher threat because it means the virus has adapted to replicate within cows' cells, which are more like human cells. The four other people diagnosed with bird flu this year in the U.S. worked on dairy farms with outbreaks.
Scientists have warned that the virus could mutate to spread from person to person, like the seasonal flu, and spark a pandemic. There's no sign of that, yet.
So far, all nine cases reported this year have been mild, consisting of eye irritation, a runny nose, and other respiratory symptoms. However, numbers remain too low to say anything certain about the disease because, in general, flu symptoms can vary among people with only a minority needing hospitalization.
The number of people who have gotten the virus from poultry or cattle may be higher than nine. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has tested only about 60 people over the past four months, and powerful diagnostic laboratories that typically detect diseases remain barred from testing. Testing of farmworkers and animals is needed to detect the H5N1 bird flu virus, study it, and stop it before it becomes a fixture on farms.
Researchers have urged a more aggressive response from the CDC and other federal agencies to prevent future infections. Many people exposed regularly to livestock and poultry on farms still lack protective gear and education about the disease. And they don't yet have permission to get a bird flu vaccine.
Nearly a dozen virology and outbreak experts recently interviewed by KFF Health News disagree with the CDC's decision against vaccination, which may help prevent bird flu infection and hospitalization.
'We should be doing everything we can to eliminate the chances of dairy and poultry workers contracting this virus,' said Angela Rasmussen, a virologist at the University of Saskatchewan in Canada. 'If this virus is given enough opportunities to jump from cows or poultry into people, it will eventually get better at infecting them.'
To understand whether cases are going undetected, researchers in Michigan have sent the CDC blood samples from workers on dairy farms. If they detect bird flu antibodies, it's likely that people are more easily infected by cattle than previously believed.
'It's possible that folks may have had symptoms that they didn't feel comfortable reporting, or that their symptoms were so mild that they didn't think they were worth mentioning,' said Natasha Bagdasarian, chief medical executive for the state of Michigan.
In hopes of thwarting a potential pandemic, the United States, United Kingdom, Netherlands, and about a dozen other countries are stockpiling millions of doses of a bird flu vaccine made by the vaccine company CSL Seqirus.
Seqirus' most recent formulation was greenlighted last year by the European equivalent of the FDA, and an earlier version has the FDA's approval. In June, Finland decided to offer vaccines to people who work on fur farms as a precaution because its mink and fox farms were hit by bird flu last year.
The CDC has controversially decided not to offer at-risk groups bird flu vaccines. Demetre Daskalakis, director of the CDC's National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases, told KFF Health News that the agency is not recommending a vaccine campaign at this point for several reasons, even though millions of doses are available. One is that cases still appear to be limited, and the virus isn't spreading rapidly between people as they sneeze and breathe.
The agency continues to rate the public's risk as low. In a statement posted in response to the new Colorado cases, the CDC said its bird flu recommendations remain the same: 'An assessment of these cases will help inform whether this situation warrants a change to the human health risk assessment.'
KFF Health News is a national newsroom that produces in-depth journalism about health issues and is one of the core operating programs at KFF—an independent source of health policy research, polling, and journalism. Learn more about KFF.

title: Credit Union of Colorado Foundation Awards $50,000 in College Scholarships
description: Credit Union of Colorado Foundation has announced the 2024 winners of its annual college scholarship program. The Foundation awarded ten students with a $5,000 annual scholarship totaling $50,000 in…
content:
Credit Union of Colorado Foundation has announced the 2024 winners of its annual college scholarship program. The Foundation awarded ten students with a $5,000 annual scholarship totaling $50,000 in tuition assistance for the 2024/2025 school year. Fort Collins winner Ariella Maroni will use the scholarship to help pay for her college education at Duke University.
'We are honored to provide financial support to college students from communities throughout Colorado,' says Phil Smith, board chair of the Credit Union of Colorado Foundation and President and CEO of Credit Union of Colorado. 'This year's recipients are not only accomplished academically but also dedicated volunteers who serve their schools and communities. The future is bright with these students who will no doubt make lasting impacts in both their careers and communities.'
Scholarship eligibility was extended to students who are Colorado residents enrolled in, or scheduled to enter, an accredited college or university as an undergraduate taking at least 12 credit hours per semester. Candidates were required to maintain a minimum 3.5 grade-point average on a 4.0 scale in high school or during the previous 12 months as a college undergraduate and demonstrate an active commitment to volunteer activities and community service at their school or in their local community.

Ariella Maroni, Fort Collins – attending Duke University

Caleb Merson, Denver – attending Colorado State University

Image by Claim Accident Services from Pixabay

Almost every Columbia personal injury lawyer states that proving liability is fundamental i n any personal injury claim. Without clear evidence to establish fault on the part of the responsible party, it becomes challenging to hold them accountable for your injuries and losses. By documenting evidence from the scene of the accident, such as photographs or videos, you can provide visual proof of what occurred. Witness statements or police reports may also serve as compelling forms of evidence when establishing liability. Proving Damages
A longside liability, documenting evidence is equally important in substantiating your damages. Personal injury claims seek compensation for both economic (medical expenses, lost wages) and non-economic ( pain and suffering , emotional distress) damages. Obtain medical records detailing your injuries and treatment history. Keep a record of all related expenses, such as medical bills and receipts for out-of-pocket costs. Receipts for property damage repairs or estimates can also aid in proving economic losses. Strengthening Your Case
A strong collection of evidence serves to strengthen your overall personal injury case by providing weighty support for your narratives and claims about what happened and who should be held responsible. Objective documentation minimizes room for falsely disputed facts or narratives that could adversely affect your position during negotiations or legal proceedings. Preserving Important Information
In civil litigation cases like personal injury claims, time isn't always on your side; important details may fade over time as memories become less reliable or witnesses become harder to find. Therefore, it is crucial to capture and preserve information while it is fresh. Documenting evidence promptly and accurately helps ensure that essential details, such as the condition of the accident scene or witness statements, remain intact. Avoiding Inaccurate Recollections
Over time, memories can become distorted or unintentionally altered. Documenting evidence helps counter these subjective recall biases that may impact accounts provided by witnesses or even your own memory. By having documented evidence in hand, you minimize the discrepancies that may arise during testimony or cross-examination. Building Credibility
Attention to detail in collecting and documenting evidence enhances your credibility as a claimant during negotiations or court proceedings. When presenting clear, organized, and compelling evidence, you demonstrate a strong commitment to seeking justice and a fair resolution. This gives weight to your case and increases the likelihood of achieving a favorable outcome. Demonstrating the Extent of Your Injuries
Personal injury claims depend on establishing how injuries have affected your life physically, emotionally, and financially. By meticulously documenting photographic evidence of injuries or keeping a journal detailing daily struggles resulting from your injuries, you effectively communicate their extent to insurance adjusters and opposing parties and potentially convince juries if necessary. Enhancing Negotiation Power
Documented evidence provides concrete support during negotiations with insurance companies or other parties involved in the personal injury claim. By presenting a strong collection of evidence, you can substantiate your demands for fair compensation. When faced with undeniable proof of liability and damages, insurance adjusters may be more inclined to offer a settlement that meets your needs rather than risk a potentially costly lawsuit. Strengthening Your Legal Representation
When you have documented evidence available, it significantly enhances the effectiveness of your legal representation . An experienced personal injury attorney can use this evidence to build a compelling case on your behalf. Your lawyer can strategically negotiate or litigate with tangible proof supporting your claims to maximize compensation and advocate for your rights. Conclusion
Documenting evidence is crucial in personal injury claims for several reasons. It helps establish liability, prove damages, and strengthen your case's narrative. Keeping accurate records preserves vital information while memories are fresh and addresses inaccuracies before disputes arise. Detailed documentation can challenge the facts of the events and build the claimant's credibility. It also demonstrates the true extent of the injuries, improving the chances of successful negotiation and fair compensation.

title: Rapids Await Archive Collection Treatment
description: Sports merchandising is a big business. Depending on the size of its fanbase, estimates place the money made from merchandising at around 5-15% of a franchise's income. The value of Lionel Messi's…
content:
https://unsplash.com/s/photos/soccer
Sports merchandising is a big business. Depending on the size of its fanbase, estimates place the money made from merchandising at around 5-15% of a franchise's income. The value of Lionel Messi's name alone has kept his replica jersey on the MLS Store at the top of the sales charts for the past two years – and, according to Sportico, has boosted gate receipts at Inter Miami by 200%. Lack of Purpose
Across the pond, the Premier League's most popular jerseys include Bukayo Saka (Arsenal), Mohamed Salah (Liverpool), and Reece James (Chelsea). James is the only player on the list who isn't a midfielder or forward. It's the goal tally that attracts fan dollars. ESPN claims that Liverpool made €132 million from shirt sales in 2023.
Inevitably, the key to more cash is more jerseys, and the traditional third kit seems to fill this need. While (apparently) necessary, research from @kit_geek on Twitter reveals that third kits were only worn 10% of the time during 2018, compared to an away kit in 17% of matches and a variation on the home strip 8% of the time. London's Tottenham Hotspur didn't use their third kit at all.
The third kit's lack of purpose has led to a trend for experimentation. Crystal Palace's third kit for 23/24 is covered in graffiti, Man City's has lightning bolts, and Spurs is a pleasant Inter Miami pink. The MLS has taken things one step further for the new campaign by introducing the Archive Collection for five teams, a set of retro-inspired third jerseys.
Unfortunately, the Rapids don't get one. The Archive Collection
Ironically, retro is one of those things that never goes out of fashion. It's a recurring urge of fashion designers, video game developers, and even movie studios, who have been dredging the past for 'new' material for a while now.
Modus Games' just brought the Double Dragon franchise (1987) back, while online casino operators have plumbed the 1980s for the slot Cash Volt . This features all the classic symbols, like BAR, lemons, cherries, and 7s. Also, for some reason, dresses from the 1950s are in vogue again.
The MLS doesn't seem to have a particular inspiration for its Archive Collection, a set of five jerseys in retro color palettes. In fact, it's not even true to its concept (Inter Miami has a Miami Dolphins-inspired shirt , despite only joining the MLS four years ago). The Rapids, along with D.C. United, Sporting Kansas City, and six others, have been playing since 1996.
Of course, as with many of the third kits mentioned earlier, the Archive Collection is another way for the MLS to separate fans from their money – a lot of it. It costs $194.99 for the Lionel Messi version of Inter Miami's shirt.
The Rapids only released a third kit in 2001 but, after switching home colors twice (in 2003 to blue and black and in 2007 to claret), Colorado has a long history of unique shirts to adorn a special edition.
Maybe next year.

title: Essential Skills Every Concierge Should Have
description: At a hotel or other hospitality business, such as a club or restaurant, the concierge is typically the first point of contact for any guest. Concierges are primarily responsible for providing guests…
content:
Source: Unsplash
At a hotel or other hospitality business, such as a club or restaurant, the concierge is typically the first point of contact for any guest.
Concierges are primarily responsible for providing guests with information about locations and services outside the hotel. For instance, a concierge may arrange accommodations, recommend local dining and entertainment, and make transportation or activity reservations on a guest's behalf.
In the hospitality industry, a concierge is the most important figure with whom the guests will interact directly.
So, if you are a recruiter at a hospitality business or someone who sees themselves as a prospective concierge, this article is for you.
Read on as we discuss the concierge job description and outline the essential hard and soft skills of a great concierge. Who Is a Concierge & What Are Their Responsibilities?
The concierge is responsible for fulfilling a wide range of guest requests — but does so seamlessly and effortlessly as if no work has been done — all while prioritizing guest satisfaction above all else.
More so, a great concierge must be well-mannered, courteous, and professional in every interaction with the hotel's guests.
Typical concierge duties and responsibilities include: assisting guests with their requests or inquiries
taking messages on behalf of guests
making reservations on behalf of guests (e.g., dinner, golf tee, play, etc.)
arranging local and airport transportation
providing information about local activities and attractions
making travel arrangements for sightseeing or other tourist activities
planning events, parties, or meetings
obtaining tickets to events
providing business services
arranging childcare services for guests
handling luggage, packages, or mail
A concierge has a wide scope of daily activities. Thus, it is only natural that being a concierge requires a diverse skill set. Skills and Qualifications of a Concierge
Concierge skills encompass a blend of hard and soft skills that enable you to cultivate strong relationships with guests, efficiently manage tasks, and consistently deliver exceptional customer service. Concierge Soft Skills
Soft skills are essential for successful concierge work as they involve your ability to interact effectively with others. Excellent Communication Skills
Being a concierge means you interact with clients, guests, and colleagues on a daily basis. Effective communication is essential for conveying messages, understanding others, and making a positive impression.
Good communication also requires being a good listener and understanding guests' needs and desires, even when they are not directly expressed. Adaptability
Adaptability involves being open to new ideas and concepts and responding quickly to ensure guest satisfaction, even in the face of unexpected challenges.
A good concierge should be able to easily adjust their approach. After all, you will meet different people with diverse expectations and unique requests, and you need to treat them all equally professionally and enthusiastically. Problem-Solving
You often find yourself in situations where you need to quickly and practically solve guests' issues or problems. Your guests may ask you for information you don't know, or a problem may come up that you are unsure how to solve.
Having strong problem-solving skills will help you evaluate the situation, identify possible options, and choose the best course of action. Self-Management
In your role as a concierge, you will be responsible for juggling multiple tasks and fulfilling various requests. Effective time management is crucial to ensuring that you can promptly complete tasks, meet guests' needs, and effectively manage stress.
Additionally, you may not have a typical supervisor, so it's important to be able to organize your time, tasks, and priorities effectively on your own. Being able to manage yourself is a crucial skill in this role. Concierge Hard Skills
In this section, we focus on the hard skills the concierge gets to develop and sharpen through schooling, training, or on-the-job experience. Knowledge of Multiple Languages
Speaking multiple languages is a significant and advantageous asset for a concierge. Chances are, your hotel will welcome numerous guests from different parts of the world, and not all of them will be well-versed in your local language or English.
Knowing at least one foreign language can help you provide better assistance to guests and offer a more personalized service. Technological Proficiency
Tech-savviness is a valuable skill for a modern concierge. Most hospitality establishments have complex booking systems, property management software, word processors, and databases — all of which represent a concierge's main tools in ensuring guest satisfaction. Good Familiarity with the Local Area
When we say good familiarity, we mean knowing the local area like the back of your hand.
Having a deep knowledge of the hotel's local area, including the finest restaurants, attractions, and activities, is a skill vital to a concierge's professional success.
Guests may have various requests, such as where to find the best local cuisine, a jazz nightclub, a reliable dogsitter, or the best hair salon. While guests can search for these answers themselves, a concierge is there to suggest better places and ones that are more suitable for their particular wishes.

title: $25 Trees Available to Fort Collins Residents Through the Community Canopy Program
description: The City of Fort Collins Forestry Division is once again partnering with Nature in the City, Fort Collins Wholesale Nursery, and the Arbor Day Foundation to provide the Community Canopy Program. This…
content:
Past Tree Planting on Colorado State University Campus - Photo courtesy of the CSFS.
The City of Fort Collins Forestry Division is once again partnering with Nature in the City, Fort Collins Wholesale Nursery, and the Arbor Day Foundation to provide the Community Canopy Program. This August, 1,000 trees will be available to residents within Fort Collins' Growth Management Area (GMA) for $25 each.
Starting at 8 a.m. on Monday, August 12, Fort Collins GMA residents can purchase trees online at fcgov.com/treecanopy. An online tool will guide participants on how to choose the most strategic planting location near their homes, offering the maximum environmental benefit and helping estimate the annual financial savings that will result from planting the trees. Residents may reserve up to two trees per household and are expected to care for and plant them in the location provided through the online tool.
All 1,000 trees are locally grown by Fort Collins Wholesale Nursery with several different species available including Bigtooth maple, Catalpa, Sucker Punch Chokecherry, varieties of oak and elm, along with other species ideal for Fort Collins' climate. The Community Canopy purchasing site will remain available online until all trees are reserved. The trees will be available for pickup on September 7 from 8 a.m.-4 p.m. at Hoffman Mill. At the time of purchase, one-hour timeslots for tree pickup reservations will be available for selection.
Community urban forests provide numerous benefits including releasing oxygen, capturing air pollutants and carbon dioxide, filtering and reducing stormwater runoff, reducing energy demand, and cooling down ambient temperatures via shade. Additionally, they sustain habitat for birds and other wildlife and contribute greatly to human and community health. Through the Community Canopy Program, homeowners can help broaden the city's tree canopy and create a more diverse and resilient urban forest.
This program is a collaborative effort brought to you by the City of Fort Collins Forestry Division and Nature in the City, a City of Fort Collins Natural Areas Department program.
About the Arbor Day Foundation
Founded in 1972, the Arbor Day Foundation has become the largest nonprofit membership organization dedicated to planting trees, with more than one million members, supporters, and valued partners. Since its inception, more than 600 million Arbor Day Foundation trees have been planted in neighborhoods, communities, cities, and forests throughout the world. 'Our vision is to lead toward a world where trees are used to solve issues critical to survival by relentlessly delivering value.'
As one of the world's largest operating conservation foundations, the Arbor Day Foundation, through its members, partners, and programs, educates and engages stakeholders and communities across the globe to involve themselves in its mission of planting, nurturing, and celebrating trees. More information is available at arborday.org.

title: Banner Health Offers New Injection Treatments for Women to Provide Relief From Urine Leakage
description: Two providers at Banner Health are now offering Bulkamid injections, a new, minimally invasive treatment for stress urinary incontinence (SUI). Emilee Sandsmark, MD, and McKenna Li, DO, are two of…
content:
Photo Courtesy of Banner Health
Two providers at Banner Health are now offering Bulkamid injections, a new, minimally invasive treatment for stress urinary incontinence (SUI). Emilee Sandsmark, MD, and McKenna Li, DO, are two of only a few practitioners in the region offering this innovative procedure. SUI affects one in three women and causes unintentional urine leakage during activities such as coughing, laughing, sneezing, or exercising.
Bulkamid, a water-based gel mixed with polyacrylamide, creates a local response with the patient's own cells to recruit cells to bulk up the area around the urethra, narrowing the natural opening of the urethra. Bulkamid is injected into the urethra under general anesthetic during a quick outpatient appointment in a regular operating room. Patients receiving the treatment are generally back home in under three hours with minimal risk and low rates of localized reaction.
'If someone comes to our office and reports leaking of urine, and we deem it is stress urinary incontinence, we offer a variety of options, including more conservative management like pelvic floor physical therapy, vaginal estrogen or vaginal weights,' Dr. Sandsmark said. 'Those are all less invasive, and patients may choose to do those treatments first. But it is also okay to move forward with a procedural correction if the patient desires.'
While the gold standard for treating SUI remains a mid-urethral sling, Bulkamid injections provide a new alternative for women looking for something more direct than non-invasive options but less risky than the mid-urethral slings.
Risks to the mid-urethral sling procedure include bleeding, nerve damage, urinary retention, and mesh erosion. In contrast, Bulkamid injections have almost no risk and provide an 80% to 90% satisfaction rate. Only 30% of women need a touch-up treatment within one year of the first treatment to achieve this high satisfaction rate. Bulkamid is clinically proven to be durable and effective for up to seven years, providing women with safe and long-lasting relief of their SUI symptoms.
'Bulkamid is the first product in the market that is thought to have lower rates of localized reaction than other bulking agents,' Dr. Sandsmark said. 'That has to do with how the agent recruits the patient's own cells to cushion the urethra, as opposed to foreign material reaction. The only real risk is that the procedure is not effective, and that is unlikely.'
Women in Northern Colorado interested in learning more about Bulkamid injections can schedule a consultation with Dr. Sandsmark at the Banner Health Clinic in Loveland by calling 970-820-2009 or Dr. Li at the Banner Health Clinic in Fort Collins at 970-821-4500.
About Banner Health
Banner Health is one of the largest secular nonprofit healthcare systems in the country. In addition to 33 hospitals, Banner also operates an academic medicine division, Banner – University Medicine, and Banner MD Anderson Cancer Center , a partnership with one of the world's leading cancer programs, MD Anderson Cancer Center. Banner's array of services includes a health insurance division, employed physician groups, outpatient surgery centers, urgent care locations, home care and hospice services, retail pharmacies, stand-alone imaging centers, physical therapy and rehabilitation, behavioral health services, a research division, and a nursing registry. To make health care easier, 100% of Banner-employed doctors are available for virtual visits, and patients may also reserve spots at Banner Urgent Care locations and can book appointments online with many Banner-employed doctors. Headquartered in Arizona, Banner Health also has locations in California, Colorado, Nebraska, Nevada and Wyoming. For more information, visit bannerhealth.com .

title: Colorado Continues To Develop Crypto-Friendly Regulations
description: In recent years, Colorado has emerged as a leading advocate for cryptocurrency and blockchain technology, establishing itself as a progressive state in the development of crypto-friendly regulations.…
content:
(Photo by Traxer on Unsplash.com)
In recent years, Colorado has emerged as a leading advocate for cryptocurrency and blockchain technology, establishing itself as a progressive state in the development of crypto-friendly regulations. The Centennial State's commitment to fostering innovation in the digital asset space reflects a broader trend toward the integration of cryptocurrency into mainstream financial and economic systems. Colorado's Early Adoption of Cryptocurrency
Colorado's journey toward becoming a crypto-friendly state began in earnest with its early adoption of cryptocurrency-related legislation and policies. Recognizing the potential of digital currencies and blockchain technology to drive economic growth and innovation, state lawmakers took proactive steps to create a conducive environment for the industry.
In 2014, Colorado became one of the first states to accept Bitcoin for tax payments, a move that highlighted the state's willingness to experiment with new financial technologies. This initiative was part of a broader effort to explore the practical applications of cryptocurrency and demonstrate its viability as a legitimate form of payment.
From here, the adoption of crypto in the state snowballed. Crypto holders can now use crypto to purchase various goods and services with digital currency. For example, Quiznos accepts crypto in exchange for meals at several places in Colorado. Similarly, crypto holders can book travel with crypto online and can play games online using crypto at offshore casino sites. Although online casino gambling remains a legal gray area in Colorado, offshore crypto casinos, like those on this crypto casino list , are often visited by gamblers in Colorado and other US states who want to wager and enjoy the benefits that crypto offers, like reduced fees and quick transactions. Beyond booking travel, playing games, and paying taxes, crypto can also be used to purchase items from e-commerce stores and even pay for experiences, like concerts. Regulatory Developments and Legislative Initiatives
Colorado's regulatory approach to cryptocurrency has been characterized by a focus on clarity, innovation, and consumer protection. Several key legislative and regulatory developments have shaped the state's crypto-friendly environment.
In 2019, Colorado passed House Bill 19-1234, which provided a legal framework for the use of blockchain technology in record-keeping and smart contracts. This legislation aimed to enhance the state's legal infrastructure for digital assets and streamline processes related to blockchain-based transactions. The bill also established guidelines for the use of blockchain in government operations, further demonstrating the state's commitment to technological advancement.
Building on this momentum, Colorado continued to refine its approach to cryptocurrency regulation with the introduction of additional legislation. For example, in 2021, Colorado Governor Jared Polis signed a bill that clarified the state's stance on digital asset taxation. The legislation aimed to address uncertainties surrounding the taxation of cryptocurrency transactions and provide clear guidance for taxpayers and businesses. This move was seen as a significant step towards creating a more transparent and predictable regulatory environment for digital assets. Encouraging Innovation Through Regulatory Sandboxes
One of the most notable aspects of Colorado's regulatory approach is its use of regulatory sandboxes to encourage innovation in the cryptocurrency space. A regulatory sandbox is a controlled environment that allows businesses and startups to test new products and services under regulatory supervision without facing the full range of regulatory requirements.
In 2020, Colorado established its own regulatory sandbox program to support the development of blockchain and cryptocurrency-related technologies. The program provides a framework for companies to test their innovations while working closely with state regulators to ensure compliance with existing laws and regulations. Supporting Crypto Businesses and Startups
Colorado's supportive regulatory environment has been instrumental in attracting and nurturing crypto businesses and startups. The state's proactive approach to legislation and regulation has created a favorable climate for companies operating in the digital asset space.
In addition to regulatory sandboxes, Colorado has implemented various programs and initiatives to support crypto businesses. For example, the Colorado Office of Economic Development and International Trade (OEDIT) has actively engaged with blockchain and cryptocurrency companies to promote investment and job creation in the state. The office provides resources and assistance to startups, helping them navigate the regulatory landscape and connect with potential investors. Looking Ahead: Future Prospects for Colorado's Crypto Regulations
Colorado is already leading the way in crypto adoption, with holders able to pay taxes with crypto, purchase food, pay for travel, play games at offshore casinos , and more. However, many believe this is just the beginning and that Colorado has a bright future with crypto.
As cryptocurrency and blockchain technology continue to evolve, Colorado is likely to remain at the forefront of regulatory development. The state's commitment to supporting innovation and creating a favorable environment for digital assets positions it well for future advancements in the industry.
In the coming years, Colorado may see further refinement of its regulatory framework to address emerging trends and challenges in the crypto space. This could include updates to legislation related to digital asset securities, privacy concerns, and cross-border transactions. Additionally, ongoing collaboration between regulators, industry stakeholders, and policymakers will be essential in ensuring that Colorado remains a leader in crypto-friendly regulations.

title: Understanding the Cost of a Facelift: What to Expect
description: When considering a facelift procedure, it's important for individuals to be aware of the cost involved. Having a clear understanding of what to expect in terms of financial investment allows for…
content:
Photo by Karolina Kaboompics: https://www.pexels.com/photo/light-blue-one-use-medical-protective-masks-4197562/
When considering a facelift procedure, it's important for individuals to be aware of the cost involved. Having a clear understanding of what to expect in terms of financial investment allows for proper planning and ensures that there are no surprises along the way. In this guest post, we will delve into the various factors that contribute to the cost of a facelift, helping readers gain insight and make informed decisions. 1. Surgeon's Expertise and Reputation
The expertise and reputation of the surgeon performing the facelift have a significant impact on the cost. Highly acclaimed surgeons with extensive experience may charge higher fees due to their skill set and track record. It is essential to do thorough research and select a reputable surgeon who specializes in facelifts to ensure desirable results. While this may incur an additional facelift cost , it is an investment in safety and quality outcomes. 2. Geographical Location
Another factor that affects the cost of a facelift is geographical location. Practices located in metropolitan or affluent areas often have higher overhead costs, resulting in higher procedure fees. On the other hand, practices located in smaller towns or rural areas tend to have lower overall expenses and therefore offer more affordable pricing options. 3. Type and Extent of Surgery
The specific type of facelift being performed also plays a role in determining cost. There are different types available, including traditional facelifts, mini-lifts, and neck lifts – all varying in complexity and procedural time. The extent of surgery required also affects pricing, as additional procedures like eyelid lifts or brow lifts may be necessary for comprehensive rejuvenation. 4. Facility Fees
Facility fees cover various expenses related to undertaking surgery at specific locations such as hospitals or surgical centers accredited by relevant governing bodies like JCI or AAAASF (Joint Commission International or American Accreditation Association for Ambulatory Health Care) respectively. These fees contribute to the overall cost of a facelift and ensure a safe environment for the procedure, including access to advanced medical equipment and staff. 5. Anesthesia Costs
During a facelift procedure, anesthesia is administered to ensure patient comfort and optimize surgical outcomes. Anesthesia costs can vary depending on factors such as the type of anesthesia used and the length of the procedure. General anesthesia, which puts patients in a fully unconscious state, tends to be more expensive compared to local or intravenous sedation. 6. Pre and Post-operative Care
Pre- and post-operative care are essential components of successful facelift surgery. They involve consultations, medical tests, overnight stays (if required), medications, check-ups, dressings, and any potential complications that may arise during recovery. These aspects add to the overall cost but are crucial for ensuring optimal results and minimizing risks. 7. Miscellaneous Expenses
It's important not to overlook miscellaneous expenses when calculating the cost of a facelift. These may include garments designed explicitly for post-operative care, prescription medications recommended by your surgeon before or after surgery, lab work if necessary, or any other ancillary fees that might arise during the process. Understanding these factors contributing to the cost of a facelift will assist readers in being adequately prepared when considering this procedure. 8. Financing Options
For individuals considering a facelift, the cost may seem overwhelming. However, it's important to note that there can be different financing options available to make the procedure more affordable. Some surgeons offer payment plans or work with healthcare financing companies that specialize in cosmetic procedures. These options allow patients to pay for their facelift over time, easing the financial burden. 9. Value Over Cost
While cost is an essential aspect to consider when undergoing a facelift, it is equally vital to focus on value rather than solely selecting based on price. A budget-friendly option does not always guarantee satisfactory results or patient safety. Opting for a skilled and experienced surgeon who meets your expectations and provides desired outcomes is crucial in ensuring both physical transformation and peace of mind throughout the process. In Conclusion
It's vital for those contemplating a facelift procedure to have an understanding of all associated costs involved in order to make informed decisions confidently. By taking into account factors such as surgeon expertise and reputation, geographical location, type and extent of surgery required, facility fees, anesthesia costs, pre-and post-operative care expenses, as well as any miscellaneous items necessary for successful recovery, it becomes possible to determine an approximate budget for this transformative journey towards self-confidence renewal through facial rejuvenation.
